audit.whatIsWrong: CHAMP_FULL calls this FAVOURED at 4/10 and gives Rumble 5 of 7 phase sides, while the content level chart and the Emerald+ data give Kled levels 2 through first item and a 48.68% win rate over 378 games.
audit.why: The two layers contradict each other and the data. Kled's Bear Trap on a Rope (11/10/9/8/7s) plus Jousting (13/12/11/10/9s) re-threaten faster than Flamespitter (10/9/8/7/6s) recycles, and Rumble has no dash to leave a committed trade.
audit.corrected: Roughly even lane, ~6/10 difficulty. Rumble owns level 1 only; Kled leads from 2 through the first item; late is execution.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes referenced 'Beartrap on a Rope' (fabricated spelling) and never gave a cooldown number for any spike.
audit.why: Kled's real spikes are level 2 (Bear Trap on a Rope), level 3 (Violent Tendencies four-attack burst), level 6 (Chaaaaaaaarge!!! at 140s rank 1) and first item; Rumble's are levels 2-3 and Liandry's.
audit.corrected: Named the real abilities and attached rank-1 cooldowns (trap 11s, Jousting 13s, Chaaaaaaaarge!!! 140s, The Equalizer 130s rank 1 / 80s rank 3).

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Bear Trap on a Rope hooks first and only yanks if the target stays shackled a short duration. Nothing in either layer told the player how to break it. Electro Harpoon's magic-resist shred was also never connected to Flamespitter.
audit.why: Riot's own text: the trap 'hooks an enemy champion. If shackled for a short duration, the target takes additional physical damage and is yanked toward Kled.' Scrap Shield (flat 6s) grants a burst of movement speed and is Rumble's only distance tool. Electro Harpoon explicitly reduces Magic Resist, so both charges before Flamespitter is strictly more damage than after.
audit.corrected: Stated both: Scrap Shield's speed burst breaks the tether before the yank, and both harpoons land before the Q cone, not after.

audit.whatIsWrong: Trading advice said 'double-E slow if he runs' with no mention of shred ordering, and ignored the dismount state entirely.
audit.why: Dismounted Kled deals less damage to champions and his Q becomes Pocket Pistol, which knocks Kled backwards — that is Rumble's window, not Kled's.
audit.corrected: Reordered the combo (E-E then Q) and named the dismount window.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown breakdown listed 'Your committal tool' and 'Your ultimate' generically with no numbers.
audit.why: Concrete numbers make the advice actionable and are the point of this section.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Let him remount' was listed as a mistake, paired with a description about burning a cooldown for tiny value — the two do not match.
audit.why: The mismatched pair reads as filler and teaches nothing.
audit.corrected: Rewrote to 'Chase a remount' with the real reason: Skaarl at full courage restores his champion damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Kit-file derived flags mark Rumble's Scrap Shield as 'knockup' and 'terrain'.
audit.why: Riot's description for Scrap Shield is a shield plus a burst of move speed — no displacement, no terrain. The flags are tooltip-parsing misfires and _missing-interactions.json inherits them.
audit.corrected: Not asserted anywhere in the rewrite; Scrap Shield is used only as shield plus speed burst.

edits.before: Level 1 is the one window you actually own in this lane. Kled has no Beartrap on a Rope yet — walk Flamespitter straight into him, stay in the Danger Zone, and take free HP. The moment he hits Level 2 the math shifts: Beartrap on a Rope roots you in place and his mounted Q drag pulls you into sustained trade range where his damage trades even or better. Dodge that tether every time — sidestep laterally rather than backing straight out, because the projectile has travel time. If you eat a root, Scrap Shield immediately and double Electro-Harpoon to burn his mounted follow-up.
edits.after: Level 1 is the one window you own outright. Kled has no Bear Trap on a Rope yet — walk Flamespitter straight into him, hold the cone for its full 3 seconds in Danger Zone, and take free HP. At 2 the maths shifts: the trap hooks you and only yanks you in if the leash holds, so the counterplay is distance. Sidestep laterally, because the trap is a travelling projectile, and if it sticks, Scrap Shield instantly — the speed burst is on a flat 6 seconds and it is the one tool that breaks the tether before the pull. Then land both Electro Harpoons; the magic-resist shred is what makes your follow-up Flamespitter actually hurt.

edits.before: Kled owns the mid-lane phase hard. His mounted aggression and Beartrap on a Rope root make every extended trade dangerous for you — you have no mobility tool to escape once he commits, and if he dismounts he simply remounts after you burn your cooldowns chasing. Farm safely by keeping Flamespitter range without over-committing into tether range. Use Level 6 Equalizer as a defensive deterrent rather than aggression — place it across the lane when he steps up to trade, forcing him to walk through rocket damage or disengage. That slows him enough to reset the trade.
edits.after: Kled owns this phase. Bear Trap on a Rope is down to 8-9 seconds and Jousting to 11-12, so he re-threatens faster than Flamespitter comes back, and you have no dash to leave once he commits. Farm at the edge of your 600 cone and never inside trap range with Scrap Shield already spent — that shield is your tether break, not a damage buffer. Dismounted Kled deals reduced damage to champions and his Q becomes Pocket Pistol, which knocks him backwards: that is your kill window, not his. At 6 use The Equalizer defensively, laid across his step-up so he walks through burn and slow to reach you.

edits.before: The late game is genuinely even. Kled's R charge can be baited — when you see him channel his ultimate, drop Equalizer on his landing zone to deal massive damage and force him into it already slowed and burning. Your global Equalizer presence in teamfights is something Kled cannot replicate: you can fire it cross-map while he has to be on top of the fight. In side-lane 1v1s he still wins the raw brawl, so avoid isolated fights without escape routes, and make your value cross-map with your R rather than trying to match his skirmish output.
edits.after: The late game is genuinely even. Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is a 140-second commit at rank 1 and travels 3500 units, so bait it and drop The Equalizer on his landing zone — he arrives already slowed and burning. Your Equalizer at 80 seconds fires from 1750 range across a fight Kled has to be physically standing in; that reach is the thing he cannot copy. In isolated side-lane 1v1s he still wins the raw brawl, so refuse fights without an exit and take your value cross-map with R rather than trying to match his skirmish output.

notes: Rumble's Scrap Shield carries derived flags "knockup" and "terrain" in champ-data/_kits/rumble.json; Riot's own description is a shield plus a burst of move speed only. Those flags are tooltip-parsing misfires, and _missing-interactions.json inherits them (it claims Scrap Shield denies dashes). Nothing in this rewrite asserts displacement or terrain from Scrap Shield. The Equalizer's "terrain" flag is likewise a misfire on the word "wall" — Riot describes a wall of flames that damages and slows, i.e. a zone, not collision that blocks dashes. Not asserted either. UNRESOLVED BY DESIGN: CHAMP_FULL phases[].side gives Rumble 5 of 7 stages while the content level chart and the 48.68% win rate give Kled levels 2 through first item. Side values are single words ("Rumble"/"Kled"/"Skill") and cannot be changed inside the +/-10% length band, so they are left untouched and flagged here. Same for full.diff ("FAVOURED", 8 chars) and full.diffRating ("4/10"); I corrected the difficulty claim in breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t instead. Someone with write access to those fields should flip phases 2-6 to Kled and diff to EVEN.
